author: Moreyra et al.
title: A thorny tale: The origin and diversification of Cirsium
published_support: Rapid radiation in Japan/NA; incongruent histories potentially ILS/hybridization
design_transfer: broad genus scaffold and taxon reconciliation
claim_limit: Not true spine or ecological fitness evolution

author: Siniscalchi et al.
title: Diversification and Biogeography of North American Thistles
published_support: Precipitation/semiaridity associated with diversification; no detected morphology-related rate increase
design_transfer: separate lineage diversification from trait evolution; independent comparison radiation
claim_limit: No O x true spine function; morphology test is not evidence of no selection

author: Chang et al.
title: Phylotranscriptomics and genome-size evidence clarify Taiwanese Cirsium complex
grain: 37 thistle accessions; morphology incl phyllary dimensions
published_support: Eastern Asian lineage delimitations and measured spine-tip classes (>3 mm vs often <2 mm) and phyllary tiering
design_transfer: real spine measurement precedent; cytotype and phylogenetic sampling companion
claim_limit: Not quantified spine access or defense fitness for focal Japanese contrasts

author: Oguro and Sakai
title: Relation between flower head traits and florivory in Asteraceae
grain: 18 species; bud/flower/fruit stages; biochemistry and head size/count
published_support: Large/more heads and nutrient/water chemistry related to attack; stage-specific phylogenetic signals
design_transfer: critical direct overlap; retain head size, nutrients and head count as alternative mechanisms
claim_limit: No head gravity angle or true spine, no same-head perturbation

author: Song et al.
title: Multifunctionality of angiosperm floral bracts: a review
published_support: Bracts multifunctional across rain/UV/herbivory/pollinators; agents vary with ontogeny
design_transfer: shows multi-function and developmental stage itself is not novel
claim_limit: Not a Cirsium-specific coupled evolutionary causal test

author: Wu and Yahara
title: Recurved Taraxacum phyllaries function as a floral defense
grain: 8 paired hybrid versus native Taraxacum contrasts; phyllary removal
published_support: Recurved bracts impede slug florivory; removal erases residence-time contrast
design_transfer: direct family-level analog for bract access routes and sham safety
claim_limit: Not Cirsium spines nor insects as ovipositors; broad historical coevolution inference less causal

author: Chen et al.
title: A nodding capitulum enhances reproductive success of Cremanthodium campanulatum
grain: alpine nodding capitula artificially held erect
published_support: Erect treatment fewer achenes; rainfall/UV pollen damage; no detected visitor preference
design_transfer: direct inflorescence orientation causal analogy; use rain/UV and filled achenes
claim_limit: Not Cirsium; could not separate independently nodding from long bracts as historical adaptive units

author: Shibata et al.
title: Flower movement induced by weather-dependent tropism satisfies attraction and protection
published_support: Facing up in sun aids visitors; facing down in rain protects flowers; reproductive outcome
design_transfer: test weather-driven movements separately from ontogenetic shifts in Cirsium
claim_limit: Not Cirsium; distinct mechanism, cannot infer same auxin control

author: Ohashi and Yahara
title: Effects of variation in flower number on pollinator visits in Cirsium purpuratum
grain: Latin square artificially arranged field plants
published_support: Bumblebee plant-level visits increase decelerating; heads/plant visitation can differ
design_transfer: record plant display and head-level pollination separately
claim_limit: Not orientation, spine or directly measured viable seeds in same experiment

author: Ohashi and Yahara
title: Effects of flower production and predispersal seed predation on reproduction in Cirsium purpuratum
published_support: Seed predation grows with flower production; more flowers need not yield more relative seed success
design_transfer: plant-level display and enemy load essential confounders
claim_limit: Population observational/model comparison; not O x spine causation
source_access: author original PDF first page screenshot and text

author: Thomas
title: Sticky Exudates on the Inflorescences of Cirsium Discolor and Penstemon Digitalis as Possible Defense Against Seed Predators
published_support: No detected increase in seed predators nor decrease in seed output after neutralizing traps
design_transfer: competition to simple defense hypothesis; sticky != spine
claim_limit: Nondetection not equality; species and site conditional

author: Reville et al.
title: Tephritid Fly Abundance and Inflorescence Herbivory on a High Alpine Thistle Vary with Environment
published_support: Three tephritid guilds partition habitats; 91.5-98.5% head seed damage; 8.2% vs 1.6% viable seed proportion
design_transfer: partner-regime hypothesis with individual/site pseudoreplication controls
claim_limit: one season/three sites and 9 plants; no spine or orientation interventions; habitat not isolated from elevation

author: Hibbins et al.
title: Phylogenomic comparative methods: Accurate evolutionary inferences in presence of gene tree discordance
published_support: Ignoring discordant trees can bias floral trait rates/ASR
design_transfer: use tree ensemble and network sensitivity where gene discordance in Cirsium
claim_limit: Does not solve network/reticulation by simple substitution of one RAD tree

author: Cooper et al.
title: A cautionary note on use of Ornstein Uhlenbeck models in macroevolutionary studies
published_support: OU favored spuriously by small trees/data errors
design_transfer: power and adequacy simulation prerequisite; no naked AICc optimum claim
claim_limit: OU is stochastic model not causal demonstration of selection

author: Pienaar et al.
title: Phylogenetic comparative methods for studying adaptation: the adaptation-inertia framework
published_support: OU interpretation can use environment-associated moving optima and phylogenetic inertia
design_transfer: advanced extension only when independently estimated ecological regimes/traits support it
claim_limit: review not data, 38-tip tree likely insufficient for heavy multivariate regimes

author: Platycodon flower orientation authors
title: Horizontal orientation facilitates pollen transfer and rain damage avoidance in Platycodon grandiflorus
grain: one field population + in vitro pollen rain test
published_support: Horizontal flowers gain pollinator/stigma loads vs other angles and avoid wet pollen loss vs upward
design_transfer: do not presume downward always best; allow intermediate optima and niche-specific responses
claim_limit: Not Cirsium; reproductive geometry differs

author: Armbruster and Muchhala
title: Floral reorientation: restoration of pollination accuracy after accidents
published_support: Rapid reorientation common in bilateral flowers; radial flowers mostly not
design_transfer: separate developmental change/weather-driven from compensatory injury correction
claim_limit: Cirsium heads are not equivalent to single bilateral corollas

author: West and Louda team
title: Inconsistent annual compensation for floral herbivory by an iterocarpic thistle
grain: apical damage and floral herbivory in two seasons
published_support: Late heads partially compensate; whole-plant seed output not consistently improved
design_transfer: distinguish head stage local effects from full maternal fitness; annual replication
claim_limit: Study not about phyllary spine or gravity angle

author: Cirsium pitcheri study
title: Effect of capitulum position and weevil infestation on seed production of threatened monocarpic perennial Cirsium pitcheri
published_support: Infestation differs by head position; weevil infested heads produced fewer mature seeds
design_transfer: head rank as a covariate for true orientation tests
claim_limit: capitulum position on plant not orientation under gravity

author: Willson, Anderson & Thomas
title: Bracteal Exudates in Two Cirsium Species as Possible Deterrents to Insect Consumers of Seeds
grain: Illinois 1980 and Minnesota 1980/82 cohorts; original original-individual sample count not verified
published_support: Indexed original study abstract reports higher seed predation when C. discolor stickiness occluded; no detected effect for C. flodmanii
design_transfer: high-value conflict with Thomas 2003; guild/site/year dependent conditional defense hypothesis
claim_limit: Second-hand indexed original abstract only, full original source and head denominators not authenticated

author: Thomas
title: Arthropods Utilizing Sticky Inflorescences of Cirsium Discolor and Penstemon Digitalis
grain: qualitative arthropod observations not randomized fitness manipulations
published_support: Pollinators avoided sticky surface; seed predators could bypass; ants and aphids deterred; some arthropod predators gleaned trapped insects
design_transfer: measure actual pathway/contact and guild: sticky presence does not equal filter of legitimate visitor or seed predator
claim_limit: No demonstrated causal seed-fitness benefit from behavioral observations alone
